root_cause.text: In the MCTP I2C receive path, mctp_i2c_recv() allocates an skb but fails to release it when midev->allow_rx is false, because the drop branch assumes netif_rx() will consume the packet even though it is never called there.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `kfree_skb(skb);` specifically in the `else` branch where `status = NET_RX_DROP` and `midev->allow_rx` is false, and the commit message states that in this case “the newly allocated skb isn't consumed by netif_rx(), it needs to free the skb directly.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the dropped receive skb in mctp_i2c_recv to prevent a memory leak on the NET_RX_DROP path.
intent_record.what: A call to kfree_skb(skb) was added in the else branch after spin_unlock_irqrestore(&midev->lock, flags), where status is set to NET_RX_DROP.
intent_record.how: When packet reception falls into the drop path, the socket buffer is now explicitly freed instead of being left allocated, preventing a memory leak during dropped receive handling.

grouping_result.intent: Free the dropped receive skb in mctp_i2c_recv to prevent a memory leak on the NET_RX_DROP path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the described root cause by freeing the receive skb in mctp_i2c_recv when allow_rx is false and the packet is dropped, preventing the memory leak on the drop path.

candidates.rationale: This drop-path assignment is the direct trigger for the leak: when allow_rx is false, execution sets NET_RX_DROP and exits the branch without passing the skb to netif_rx() or freeing it.
This conditional means only the success path hands ownership to netif_rx(); for NET_RX_DROP the skb is neither consumed nor freed, embodying the faulty assumption behind the leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement marks the packet as dropped when receive is not allowed, but does not free the allocated skb. Because the drop path never calls netif_rx(), ownership is not transferred and the skb leaks.
This condition restricts skb handoff to the success path only. When status is NET_RX_DROP, the code skips netif_rx() and, without a corresponding free, leaves the allocated skb unreleased.

    mctp i2c: MCTP I2C binding driver
    
    Provides MCTP network transport over an I2C bus, as specified in
    DMTF DSP0237. All messages between nodes are sent as SMBus Block Writes.
    
    Each I2C bus to be used for MCTP is flagged in devicetree by a
    'mctp-controller' property on the bus node. Each flagged bus gets a
    mctpi2cX net device creat
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of the relevant function `mctp_i2c_recv()` and clearly shows the vulnerable logic. After validating the frame, it allocates an skb with `skb = netdev_alloc_skb(ndev, recvlen);`. It then checks `midev->allow_rx` under the lock: `if (midev->allow_rx) { ... status = netif_rx(skb); ... } else { status = NET_RX_DROP; ... }`. In the `else` branch, `netif_rx(skb)` is not called, and there is also no `kfree_skb(skb)` or other skb release before returning. The later status handling only updates stats: `if (status == NET_RX_SUCCESS) { ... } else { ndev->stats.rx_dropped++; } return 0;`, which does not free the skb. This matches the stated root cause exactly: when `allow_rx` is false, the code assumes the drop path is sufficient but leaks the allocated skb because ownership is never transferred to `netif_rx()` and the skb is never released. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present.
